title: South32 sees limited risk of Indonesia replicating nickel success in alumina
body: South32 reported a 75% surge in full-year profit on Thursday, helped by strong performance at its alumina division and higher commodity prices.

title: Freeport Indonesia to wrap up Gresik plant repairs by early September
body: Freeport expects to complete early next month repair work at its JV smelter in East Java.

title: Indonesia scraps coal pricing rules after pushback from buyers
body: Miners will now be allowed to sell below government-set benchmarks.

title: Freeport Indonesia to ramp up concentrate exports ahead of ban
body: The firm has exported about 65% of the quota as of mid-August.

title: Indonesia president signals intention to go after illegal mines
body: Indonesia will move to “rectify” illegal mines estimated to have caused $19 billion in state losses.

title: Nickel surpasses coal as Indonesia’s top export, Macquarie says
body: Earnings from overseas sales of nickel products were $16.5 billion in the first half of the year.

title: Indonesia discussing strategic management of critical minerals trade
body: Indonesia is one of only a only a handful of countries to strike a deal with Washington to lower US tariffs.

title: Indonesia mining ministry proposes 18 development projects for Danantara funding
body: Danantara is Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto's main vehicle to achieve his 8% economic growth target by 2029.

title: Vale Indonesia to seek up to $1.2 billion financing in 2026-2027
body: The first round of financing, around $500 million, will likely come from bank loans in early 2026.

title: Indonesian Nickel Mining Sector Faces Challenges from Illegal Mining and Environmental Concerns
body: The Indonesian nickel mining sector is struggling with the issue of illegal mining, which is hindering the implementation of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) principles and causing environmental damage and social unrest. The Indonesian Nickel Mining Association (APNI) is working to address these issues by reviewing and synchronizing 57 regulations and engaging with stakeholders, including local communities and NGOs, to develop a realistic roadmap for decarbonization.

title: Asosiasi Penambang Nikel Indonesia Holds Training to Miners 2025, Receives Positive Response from National Mining Industry Players
body: The Training to Miners (TTM) APNI 2025 event, held by the Indonesian Nickel Miners Association, provided valuable insights and updates on regulations and industry conditions, with participants expressing appreciation for the event's informative content. The event highlighted the challenges faced by the mining sector, including increasing regulatory pressures and declining commodity prices, which are affecting profit margins and requiring companies to adapt to remain competitive.

title: Indonesian Mining Industry Faces Challenges Amid Global Dynamics, with Nickel and Coal Sectors Experiencing Significant Slowdown
body: The Indonesian mining industry, particularly the nickel and coal sectors, is experiencing a significant slowdown due to global price dynamics and geopolitical factors, with nickel production reaching 250 million tons annually and coal reserves valued at US$3-4 trillion. Despite the challenges, the gold sector is showing a positive trend, with profits reaching Rp5.1 trillion as of June 2025, and the industry is urged to enhance its competencies and adapt to environmental, social, and governance (ESG) challenges to remain competitive.

title: Presiden Prabowo Subianto announces plans to eradicate illegal mining practices in Indonesia, targeting 1,063 illegal mines with potential state losses of at least Rp300 trillion.
body: The Indonesian government will take concrete steps to address illegal mining, including dismantling 1,063 identified illegal mines, with a focus on bringing to justice those involved, including high-ranking officials and elites. The move aims to reclaim the country's natural resources, boost the economy, and create quality jobs, particularly in the downstream sector, while also strengthening the rule of law and combating corruption.

title: Harga Mineral Acuan Nikel Turun Tipis di Periode Kedua Agustus 2025
body: The Harga Mineral Acuan (HMA) for nickel in the second period of August 2025 has been set at US$15.012,67 per dry metric ton, a slight decrease from the previous period. This adjustment may impact the strategies of nickel industry players, considering the HMA is a key reference for domestic transactions and royalty calculations, with prices for low-grade nickel ore also being released as a guide for transactions between miners and smelters.

title: Wakil Menteri ESDM Tekankan Pentingnya Hilirisasi Mineral untuk Meningkatkan Daya Saing Industri
body: Wakil Menteri Energi dan Sumber Daya Mineral Yuliot Tanjung menegaskan bahwa hilirisasi mineral, khususnya nikel, merupakan langkah strategis untuk meningkatkan daya saing industri dan menarik investasi, dengan pemerintah menyusun skema percepatan realisasi dan pertahanan energi nasional melalui prosedur yang mempermudah pelaku usaha dalam pengambilan keputusan investasi. Pemerintah juga telah merevisi regulasi melalui UU No. 2 Tahun 2025 yang memperkuat ketentuan keberlanjutan, seperti kewajiban pemulihan lingkungan pascatambang dan program pemberdayaan masyarakat.

title: Asosiasi Penambang Nikel Indonesia Supports Development of Sustainability Certification to Strengthen ESG Practices and Expand International Market Access
body: The Indonesian Nickel Miners Association (APNI) has expressed its readiness to support the development of sustainability certification in the mining sector to enhance environmental, social, and governance (ESG) practices and expand access to international markets. APNI is focusing on three main international standards, including the Global Integrated Mining Protocol (GIMP), which has been found to have a 78% compatibility with the IRMA standard and 90% with national regulations.

title: Nilai Ekonomi Karbon membuka peluang ekonomi baru dan meningkatkan efisiensi energi di Indonesia
body: Implementasi Nilai Ekonomi Karbon (NEK) di Indonesia membuka peluang ekonomi baru, termasuk pasar kredit karbon dan penguatan daya saing industri, serta meningkatkan efisiensi energi dan mengurangi emisi gas rumah kaca. Dengan demikian, Indonesia dapat memperoleh pendapatan negara dari pajak karbon, akselerasi teknologi bersih, dan meningkatkan ketahanan ekonomi rumah tangga terhadap fluktuasi harga energi di masa depan.

title: Vale Indonesia Commits to Sustainable Mining Practices and Environmental Conservation
body: Vale Indonesia has made significant progress in its sustainability efforts, having reclaimed 3,800 hectares of land in Sulawesi and planted 5 million trees, while also reducing its reliance on fossil fuels through the use of renewable energy sources, including three hydroelectric power plants with a total capacity of 365 MW. The company's commitment to environmental conservation and sustainability is reflected in its reduction of greenhouse gas emissions by 838,000 tons of CO₂ equivalent from 2022 to 2024, exceeding its target of 711,000 tons.

title: MIND ID Strengthens Strategic Role in Building Sustainable Industrial Ecosystem through Mineral Hilirisasi
body: MIND ID, through PT Indonesia Asahan Aluminium (INALUM), is promoting the hilirisasi of bauksit to produce high-value aluminium, with the value increasing from $40 to $2,800 after processing. The company aims to fully utilize domestic alumina by 2025, in line with the implementation of the Minerba law, while also supporting the national decarbonization agenda by reducing greenhouse gas emissions through the use of Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG).

title: PT Pertamina Hulu Energi Offshore North West Java achieves significant increase in oil production with 570 barrels per day from the UA-9 well in the Uniform field.
body: The UA-9 well, which was drilled using directional drilling, exceeded its initial production target of 276 barrels per day, with a water cut of only 5% and a flow pressure of 710-750 psig. The project was completed in 24 days, below the estimated 33.6 days, with a total cost of USD 6.15 million, approximately 60% of the approved budget.

title: Indonesia's mining and energy sector faces investment decline due to regulatory uncertainty and security concerns
body: The Indonesian government needs to create a conducive investment climate by simplifying and stabilizing regulations, ensuring fair law enforcement, and providing investment protection to attract investors in the energy and mineral sector. Failure to do so may result in decreased production, reduced state revenue, and increased unemployment, ultimately hindering the country's economic growth.
